Oh jeez, both our kids went through the Suzuki method and I spent literally years sitting through lessons and nightly practice. Four things I'd recommend for all beginners:

  1. Get a chin rest and cloth and become comfortable holding the violin under your chin without a hand for support.

  2. Make sure the bow hair is right angle to the strings

  3. Bow elbow up, approximately shoulder height

  4. Make sure your wrists don't collapse, both of them. Find some good examples of how to properly hold the bow and the neck of the instrument. Collapsed wrists is probably the hardest bad habit to break later on.

The assumption is that you can already read music and have at least some ear for pitch. If you're tone deaf then pick another instrument. If you can't read music then find some beginners music theory material and dig in.

It goes without saying that a teacher is the best way of course.

I would write out the notes under them on the page so that I could learn to "read" and identify the notes (ei: E1/C3). Once you can read the music and correlate finger placement, remove the markings a few each day or week until the board is all clean. Good luck!
